activities.title: Credit risk management
activities.timing: Daily risk alerts and weekly credit-limit monitoring. New-customer follow-ups occur after six months or in the annual cycle; blocked orders and risk events trigger ad hoc reviews.
activities.detail: Review customer credit limits and risk, resolve credit-held orders and apply the appropriate market review process.
activities.sourceExcerpt:
| Credit risk management | 1. New customer credit risk assessment (on-boarding issues)
2. Periodical Review (based on next review date)
3. Credit limit utilization monitoring
4. Credit Held order block (insufficient credit limit)
5. Risk alerts investigation
6. Monthly Controls | New customers
1. New customer reviews are triggered through our internal report for new customers, ad hoc MC requests, or credit-held sales orders.
2. The issue is where the customer can start before a CL is assigned, therefore leading to blocked orders. We have on-going discussion with the market about subject to credit (STC).
3. All markets follow an appropriate review process based on the size of the credit limit. However, in Europe and Alexion, a default credit limit and risk category are assigned to new customers due to volumes and blocking considerations. This process is managed by DMT. Smaller credit limits are reviewed again in six months to assess payment experience, while larger limits are reviewed in the next annual cycle.
4. For new customers with credit-held orders, the review is completed and the order release team is informed whether the order can be released.

Existing customers
1. The credit analyst reviews accounts in their market, checks the customer’s credit profile, and determines whether a simple review (credit limit < $1M) or Full review (credit limit > $1M) is required.
2. Simple review process is completed through the Global Decision Maker (GDM). GDM is a semi-automated application to accelerate accurate credit risk decision in real time through a blend of scoring methodology which includes D&B risk band (failure score, paydex etc) & AZ payment experience (ageing, DSO).
3. Full reviews require validation of customer information (a limited KYC is done at market level) and supporting documents such as sales forecasts, financial statements, payment term changes, and contracts where needed, followed by an assessment of sales trends, financial position, ageing, DSO, country risk, and D&B criteria. We will perform a deep dive into the customer’s financials and assess the customer’s credit worthiness against the credit limit required. A credit proposal is then submitted by email with supporting documents for multi-level approval under DOA 2002 (up to Group CFO) after which the data team updates the relevant credit details in SAP via service now ticketing system.

Monitor credit limit utilization
1. A weekly utilization report is shared with MC, highlighting customers above 80% or 90% of their credit limit to prevent blocked orders.
2. Based on MC feedback, the credit analyst performs a review where a limit increase is required, for example due to sales growth or new product launches.

Credit held order management
1. Depending on the value, the credit risk team would need to review the customer for an increased credit limit before the blocked order is manually released.
2. Credit-blocked orders must follow the global credit risk standard before manual release. If blocked due to insufficient credit limit, payment status may be confirmed with collections, and if payment is received in the AZ bank statement, the order can be released without approval. If there is no payment found, the order can be manually released if approved in line with GDOA 2002 based on the customer’s total exposure including the order value.
3. If an order is blocked due to overdue, the collection team must be informed and ensure that the relevant approvals according to the matrix in the credit risk standard (who can release it based on value and overdue allowance) before release.
4. Where an order is blocked due to payment terms (order PT being different to SAP PT), the order value must be checked and approval obtained from MC following the DOA 2000 before any modifications made to the PT in the sales order and address any other credit related issues before releasing the order.
5. Alexion orders are not blocked in the system due to its life-saving nature.

Risk alerts investigation
1. The team receives daily D&B alerts covering legal events, rating changes, ownership changes, and customer name changes across active global customers.
2. The objective of alerts process is for the team to identify potential credit risk / defaults.
3. Based on alerts received the credit risk team will take the necessary action or trigger an ad hoc credit review. When a credit event occurs e.g. bankruptcy and ceased trading, this is considered high priority, and the team would deactivate the customer where necessary. | 1. Approved credit limit, credit limit increase or decrease
2. Risk rating / score
3. Account placed on hold / blocked | 1. Sales forecast – we do not receive forecasts regarding customer level and monthly phasing, nor do we have access to the approved budget submission. We rely on the markets / FP&A to provide us with the forecast which is time consuming.
2. Manual credit review process – financial spreading, financial analysis, proposal write-up and approvals.
3. Manual controls process – manual SAP extraction for parameters, working file and remarks. Manual email search for supporting evidence on credit limit changes
4. New customer process Europe / Alexion. Material volume (3K a year), use GDM to complete which is still effort.
5. Blocked orders – Greece cash in advance (CIA) customers are blocked due to legacy practice | 1. AI solution underway for the credit review process
2. Implemented python solution for extraction of control parameter, working file and remarks. Agentic AI solution is underway to match CL changes to supporting emails. Potential broader scope and integration with credit review AI solution.
3. Applied default credit limit process for Europe / Alexion managed by DMT.
4. Proposed conversion of Greek CIA low risk customers to normal credit with direct debit 7-day term. Potentially free up 27 FTE days on order release activities.
5. Collaborate with International controller to engage markets / FP&A. |

1. SAP automatically creates sales orders based on the daily EDI report which interfaced by distributors.
2. When system identifies an error, the Sales Order team reviews the issue and follows up with the relevant teams to resolve the EDI errors.
a) For a missing end-customer account, the team liaises with the Distribution team to submit a request to DMT for account creation.
b) For missing pricing, the team liaises with the local market and GFS Controlling team to update the pricing details.
c) For insufficient stock, the team liaises with the Distribution team to carry out the necessary stock movements.

Manual order (sales)
The Sales Order team validates the completeness of the data and manually creates the order in SAP.
Orders are then subjected to a system credit check. The system will block an order if the customer account has an insufficient credit limit or overdue outstanding balances.
If an order is blocked:
a) For blocks due to credit limit exceeded, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance with GDOA 2002.
b) For blocks due to overdue balances, the Collection team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance to Global Credit Risk Policy.
c) For blocks due to a change in payment term, the Credit Risk team reviews the case and obtains the necessary approval in accordance with GDOA 2000.

Manual order (returns, rebates)

Alexion Specific Process Maps [3](#alexion-specific-process-maps)](#alexion-specific-process-maps) # PURPOSE The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to either create a new record or modify an existing record in the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. This includes different approaches for single record additions and updates, in addition to the potential for mass upload. During the execution of this process, a user may determine a master data update is required in order to complete an addition or modification. This SOP advises of the necessary steps to take should this be the case. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to the below audience: - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Middle Office - Embedded Finance (local, hub) - Alexion Regional Controllership # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded: | | | |----|----| | Business Process | Description | | Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR | # PROCEDURE ## Process Maps • Initiate the process when a new lease accounting record or lease accounting record modification is required. • Determine whether the lease is considered complex, and if yes, raise an AFN query with GFR. • Assess whether a mass upload is requested, and if yes, route to the GFS Global Lease Team for review. • Review the request and determine if a mass upload request is accepted by the GFS Global Lease Team. • Execute mass lease additions or modifications if the mass upload request is accepted. • Enter lease accounting details if the lease is not complex or mass upload is not requested. • Determine if additional cost allocation data is required, and if yes, request cost allocation data update. • Submit the lease accounting record for approval if no additional cost allocation is required. • Check if errors exist in the submitted record, and if yes, send back for review and correction. • Update lease accounting master data once the record is approved and error-free. E) Remeasuring an Accounting Schedule

A remeasurement event occurs due to any change to the lease agreement that requires a revaluation of the right-of-use asset. Examples include a lease renewal (extension), lease termination or modification of fixed charges.

1) In the Accounting Summary section of the Accounting page of a lease, select the ellipsis icon next to the schedule you wish to remeasure. A pop-up menu is displayed showing the available types of remeasurement.

2) Select the appropriate listed remeasurement.

3) Should the remeasurement effective date impact an exported period, there would be a need for intervention from the Global Lease Accounting team to perform unexport/unapproved prior to remeasurement of the schedule. Refer to Appendix - IFRS16 Guide on Global Lease Accounting Team Intervention in CoStar (by scenario)

E.1 Renewal/Data Correction

  • A lease renewal is an extension on an expiring lease. During the renewal process, the lessor and lessee negotiate new lease terms or remove old ones. The new commencement and expiration dates must be re-defined for the amortization schedule to recalculate and revalue the asset appropriately.

  • Data Correction is performed when there is data correction made in the expense pertaining dates and amount

  • If the schedule has a workflow status of Reviewed prior to the rent schedule being modified, the status will automatically change to Open for Preparation. Once the expense is triggered.

  • The following are true when performing a renewal action on an existing schedule:

    • The new date range must begin after the first period. If the new range is before an approved period, the system will calculate a retroactive adjustment.

      • A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event, such as a renewal, that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the

accounting schedule and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.

  • The system will automatically calculate the difference in the newly calculated Present Value and the end liability balance prior to the new date range as the liability adjustment.

  • The Asset Adjustment will default to an amount equal to the liability adjustment; however, you can still edit the Total Asset Adjustment by updating the manual adjustment field if further modifications are needed, such as adjusting for an impaired asset. Simply input the manual asset adjustment field with the desired value before saving the amortization schedule.

  • Before performing a renewal, the user must add new or extend existing fixed charges on the Expense or Revenue page of the lease.

  1. Select ‘Renewal’.

  2. Complete the required fields as appropriate including:

  1. Accounting Term Begin - Date of the execution letter/date the renewal was exercised

  2. Accounting Term End - The new lease expiration date according to the terms of the renewal.

  1. Click’ Calculate Values’

  2. Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as the present value, adjustment amounts, or implicit rates. The amortization periods prior to the new accounting begin date will be preserved. The level expense will adjust beginning on the new accounting begin date. Notice that the adjustment amount will automatically populate with the balance from the prior period.

  3. Click ‘Save & Close’.

  4. Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.

E.2 Impairment

  • Impairment is a permanent decline in the value of an asset. This situation exists when the cash flows or other benefits generated by an asset decline, as determined through a periodic assessment. For example, the lease administrator may discover that the fair value of an asset is far less than the carrying amount. Therefore, the difference between the fair value of the asset and it carrying amount would be written off. The payment terms do not change in the case of an impairment and thus the lease liability amortization remains intact.

  • Impairments can be prospective or retroactive, depending on the impairment.

    • A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the accounting schedule, and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.

  1. Select ‘Impairment’. The Remeasure – Impairment page is displayed.

  2. Complete the following required fields as appropriate:

  1. Accounting Term Begin - Date of the impairment.

  2. Accounting Term End - The same Period to date as the original expiration date.

  1. Enter a number into the Manual Asset Adjustment field. As an impairment reflects a drop in value, this should be a negative number.

  2. Click ‘Calculate Values’.

  3. Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as present value, adjustment amounts or implicit rates.

  4. Click ‘Save & Close’.

  5. Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.

E.3 Termination

When a termination event occurs, the amortization schedule needs to be updated so future payments are removed from the calculation and the remaining balance is capitalized at an accelerated pace.

The new date range typically begins the day you are notified about the termination and ends on the day of the termination. This determines how many periods by which to divide the remaining balance. Note: If the termination date falls within an exported period, Preparer should inform the Global Lease Accounting team to perform necessary action to unexport and unapprove the period prior to remeasurement of termination. For an example, assuming it is March 2023 closing, if a termination date falls within Dec 2022, preparer to move the workflow status of the lease to Open for Preparation and, inform the Global Lease Accounting team to unexport and unapprove journals from Dec 2022 to March 2023 Preparer should then be able to remeasure termination.

steps.title: Enter lease accounting details
steps.detail:
Note for Alexion:

Real estate: Global Real Estate (GRE) / CBRE will create/modify the CoStar data for all leases except for accounting schedule. AZ Global Lease Team will proceed with creation/modification of leases accounting schedule.

Note for CBRE is a global third-party vendor providing commercial real estate and facilities management services and manages Alexion’s global real estate portfolio.

Vehicle lease: Local Finance Markets to update data directly in CoStar (same as AstraZeneca).

Equipment lease (only applicable for BP70): Regional Controllership team to update data directly in CoStar.

The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system.

There may be a requirement to either create a new lease accounting record or modify an existing record (e.g. renewal, termination, impairment, or general modification). The details are given below:

Commence this process if:

New lease accounting record is required, or a

Lease accounting record modification is required

Check if lease require Accounting Issue Note (AIN) to be raised - An accounting issue with a financial impact of greater than USD 10 million (income statement or balance sheet) should be communicated to GFR. Generally, only unusual, complex or judgemental issues, and issues with a profit impact of greater than USD 20 million, will require a full AIN.

If yes, an AIN query should be raised with GFR according to their standard process. Below is the path for AIN template and process

Link

If no, the preparer should continue through the process to determine how the data should be entered in CoStar.

Check if lease is short term (less than 12 months) or low value (below USD 5,000)?

If yes, this is out of IFRS16 scope for AstraZeneca leases and Alexion Vehicle and Other Equipment leases, this should not be entered in CoStar and directly expensed instead.

If yes, this is out of IFRS16 scope for Alexion Property leases, the preparer should mark as “Not Applicable” in the lease accounting workflow on the Accounting page in CoStar.

If no, the preparer should continue through the process to determine how the data should be entered in CoStar.

Determine if a mass upload should be requested.

Note: The ability to mass upload creations or modifications is retained solely by the GFS Global Lease team. Preparers are able to request mass upload support in the event that:

Over 30 lease records need to be created or modified: or

Where an entity has over 300 active lease records in a particular asset class (property, Party vehicles or other); or

3rd party vehicle lease data sent directly to KL team as it falls within mass upload

If Yes, a mass upload request is required:

Refer to step: 8.3.3.11.4 GFS Global Lease Team review the request

If a mass upload request is accepted by the GFS Global Lease Team:

Refer to process 8.3.3.15 Execute mass lease additions or modifications for guidance on the procedure that follows.

Note: Although mass upload support is possible based on certain criteria being met, it should only be requested as a last resort. The most efficient process, even for large volumes of creations and modifications remains the direct entry method, utilising the productivity features of CoStar. For example, the ability to copy a record.

If No, a mass upload is not requested, follow the steps given below to create a new lease accounting record, or modify an existing one:

A) Real Estate Assets: Creation

The following section will discuss activities for day-to-day lease management.

A.1 Add a Building

1. Navigate to the Portfolio module. Under the Portfolio module, navigate the list pages by selecting Buildings.

Select the ‘+Add’ button to the right of the page and select ‘Building’

Fill the appropriate fields as per lease record requirements and click on ‘Launch’

Country - Selected as required country

State is a required fields for US and Canada only

Building Name - Company code Lease reference

Portfolio - AstraZeneca/ Alexion

Building Address

Template - Building

Sub-Group should be as per region.

It will navigate the user to the new building record where they can complete additional information for that building such as rentable area and building type. Click Save.

A.2 Add a Lease

Select ‘Add’ button to the right of the page in the Leases section of the created Building.

Complete the required fields as follows.

Building - This is auto populated

Tenant Legal Name - Company Code

Lease Type - Select the position for the lease contract. A lessor recognises lease payments from operating leases as income whereas a lessee recognises the right-of-use of the underlying leased asset and a lease liability representing its obligation to make lease payments.

Lease Template - Since the lease is created at the building record page, it will auto populate as a real estate lease.

Begin Date - Lease Commencement Date as per contract

End Date - Lease Expiration Date as per contract

Accounting Type - Select AP if the lease type includes ‘Lessee’ or ‘Sublessee’, select AR if lease type includes ‘Lessor’ or ‘Sublessor’

Parent Lease - Leave blank/not relevant for direct entry. Used in ETL.

Currency type - Select currency used on the lease contract

Units of Measure - Enter unit of measure if included on contract else allow CoStar to default

Click ‘Launch’. This will navigate to the new lease record abstract to fill additional information for the leased asset

AstraZeneca Lease Hierarchy - Should be Region>Subregion>Country

Alexion Lease Hierarchy - Should be Region > Subregion > Country > Company Code & Name

The ERP field denotes whether or not the lease belongs an entity that has cutover to SAP S/4HANA (documented as ‘S4’) as part of the current staged entity rollouts to S/4 HANA, replacing the ‘old’ journal entry processing via Blackline. The field is automatically populated based on the Company Code on the Allocations page and ensures that the relevant lease is directed to the appropriate SAP S/4HANA or ECC (Blackline) journal entry export processing.

Click on save button on the abstract. Now there are some areas that need to be completed under the Lease Information section.

A.3 Lease allocation which drives the journal coding for lease entries.

Enter Financial Information (Allocations)

Select ‘Allocations’ in the left of the lease reference.

Select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.

Select ‘Add Allocation’

Each segment value (See parameters mentioned below) must be populated to save allocation data. Select the blank area underneath any segment and a pencil icon will appear for the user to select.

Fill parameters to save the allocation and click on ‘Save’.

The AstraZeneca (ECC) parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre, Product Brand and Internal Order (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment).

The AstraZeneca (SAP S/4HANA) parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre or WBS (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment), Product Brand. Note: Internal Orders should no longer be used for SAP S/4HANA markets.

The Alexion parameters include Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre, Payment Company Code and Cost Percent.

AstraZeneca Allocations

Alexion Allocations:

Note 1: Enter the cost percent of the allocation segments. For the majority of the lease population, this will be 100% as the lease is allocated to a single location, activity and banner. If a lease is allocated to several activities, the user will need to continue to add allocation values until the cost percent is equal to 100%.

Note 2: The Payment Company Code should be the same as the Accounting Company Code in the majority of leases in Alexion. Payment Company Code will be used for tracking appropriate company code for payment files processed by the CBRE (lease administration) team. The Accounting Company Code is the company code value that pulls into the AJD file to post in Blackline.

A.4 Enter Expenses (To add instalment and base rent)

Select ‘Expenses’ in the left menu.

To add expenses, select ‘+Add’ or in the top menu bar. Quick add is best used for charges that are one-time or do not increase in amount.

Under Quick Add Charges, complete the Charge Detail section using the following inputs:

To enter an amount, first select in the Enter by section either the Fixed or Rate radio button.

Enter an amount or rate depending on whether fixed or rate was selected in the previous step in the Amount section.

Area - represents the area amount associated with the charge (e.g. square footage or square meters). This will auto populate based on the rentable area populated on the Details tab.

Payment Frequency - select frequency per the lease contract. Currency is also determined in this section by selecting from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.

Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.

End Date - Defaulted to the Lease Expiration Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.

Check the Estimated, Taxable, or Prorated checkboxes if the following conditions apply:

i. Estimated - Payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.

ii. Taxable - Used for rent charges that will be taxed based on tax authorities entered for the lease. Follow the steps under ‘Generate Tax Charges’.

iii. Prorated - Used to create partial payments for initial or final payment.

When account category is selected Charge Name is auto populated, If this is an initial expense, it should be reflected as original term else name should be changed in the case of a modification.

a. Select the vendor ‘Filler RE Vendor’ from the dropdown. This is the only vendor that is used in the AstraZeneca portfolio. For the Alexion portfolio the vendor can be selected from the dropdown. If the vendor does not exist, it must be added via the CoStar Company record.

b. Check the Estimated checkbox if the payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.

c. Enter a Start Amount in the Charge Generation section.

d. Specify all other details, such as:

i. Payment Frequency - Select frequency per the lease contract.

ii. Currency - Select from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.

iii. Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.

Click ‘Generate’ to generate the charge.

Review charges in the expenses schedule to confirm accuracy. Add additional charges as needed.

This is how a lease expense schedule is prepared

A5) Create an accounting schedule

Follow the steps below to create an accounting schedule.

Click on accounting navigation at the left side

In the top right, select Add to create a new accounting schedule.

Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule and Click Calculate Values.

Note: some fields will be derived from data in the abstract and will not need to be selected here.

Classification - Select IFRS16 from the dropdown data

Amortization Profile - Select IFRS16 from the dropdown data

Journal Entry Profile - Based on asset type - Select IFRS16 - Property from the dropdown data (Please note, there are separate Journal Entry Profiles starting with ‘S4’ to be used for all leases that should be exported via the SAP S/4HANA ledger)

Accounting Term Begin - Select Current Commencement Date from the dropdown data

Accounting Term End - Select Current Expiration Date from the dropdown data

Discount Rate Profile - System will suggest a best match discount rate

Payment Timing - Can be changed from the Annual Rate dropdown

Note: Journal Entry Profile available for use are as below. Selection should be based on asset type and nature of accounting event. Please ensure you select the correct profile based on whether the relevant lease has been cutover to SAP S/4HANA or not. If the lease should be directed to the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry export process, please only select journal entry profiles starting with ‘S4’. Continue to use all other journal entry profiles (i.e., not starting with ‘S4’) for all other leases. Other than the dropdown data below should not be in use.

Once clicked on Calculate Values, Save and Close.

Follow the steps below to modify lease accounting record for Real Estate Assets:

B) Real Estate Assets: Modification

B.1 Modify Expenses / Expense Accounts

To modify charges, navigate to the Expense page on the lease record.

Select the ellipsis on the relevant charge followed by ‘Edit’.

Make necessary modifications to the amount, account, notes or other detail associated with the charge.

Click ‘Apply’, followed by ‘Save and close’.

Note: To add a charge, click Quick Add and fill the charge details accordingly. There should be no overlapping dates. To delete a charge, select the ellipsis icon to the right of the given charge line followed by ‘Delete’

B.2 Review Payment Dates

Navigate to the expenses page on the lease record.

Under the Actions menu select the ellipsis on the right-hand side, followed by ‘Edit’.

Review the pay on dates to ensure accuracy.

If necessary, modify the proration/first recurring payment date by editing the charge.

Note: this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.

B.3 Enter Lease Option

Navigate to the lease record on the RE Abstract and select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.

Navigate to the Lease Options section of the abstract.

Select ‘Add’.

Enter all of the relevant option information including Option Type, Option Status, Description, Start date and End date in the Lease Option section.

Option Status - Should be set to Active, Declined or Exercised.

If the contract lists specific rents or charges associated with that option, enter the information in the Option Charge Generation section. (See Enter Expenses section for help with inputs).

Select ‘Save and Close’.

Note: this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.

B.4 Execute Lease Option

Navigate to the lease record and select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.

Navigate to the Lease Options section of the abstract.

Click the edit icon next to the option you would like to exercise.

Next to Option Status, click ‘Save and Exercise’.

Complete the fields in the exercise option wizard including updating lease dates, adding relevant supporting documentation such as an amendment, and reviewing the updated lease information.

Review the lease abstract to ensure the correct dates are reflected.

Note: this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.

C) Equipment Assets: Creation

The following section will discuss activities for day-to-day lease administration of non-real estate assets.

C.1 Add an Equipment Lease

Navigate to the Portfolio module.

Select the ‘Add’ button to the right of the page and click ‘Equipment Lease’

Complete the required fields including

Portfolio - AstraZeneca / Alexion

Supplier - According to company code and asset type

Legal Entity - Company Code

Template - Equipment Lease

Begin and end date

Currency type

Click ‘Launch’. This will navigate you to the new lease record where you can complete additional information (Client Lease ID - Lease reference, Address, Organizational hierarchy, Ownership type) to the leased asset.

The ERP field denotes whether or not the lease belongs an entity that has cutover to SAP S/4HANA (documented as ‘S4’) as part of the current staged entity rollouts to S/4 HANA, replacing the ‘old’ journal entry processing via Blackline. The field is automatically populated based on the Company Code on the Allocations page and ensures that the relevant lease is directed to the appropriate SAP S/4HANA or ECC (Blackline) journal entry export processing.

C.2 Lease Allocation which drives the journal coding for lease entries.

Enter Financial Information (Allocations)

Select ‘Allocations’ in the left of the lease reference

Select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner

Select ‘Add Allocation’

Each segment value must be populated to save allocation data. Select the blank area underneath any segment and a pencil icon will appear for the user to select

Fill all 4 parameters to save the allocation. The number of parameters to complete depend on whether the Equipment Lease is in the AstraZeneca or Alexion portfolio. The AstraZeneca parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre and/or Internal Order/WBS (Internal Order to be removed after all entities are leveraging the new integration to SAP S/4HANA), Product Brand and Cost Percent. The Alexion parameters include Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre, Payment Company Code and Cost Percent.

Click on Save.

AstraZeneca Allocations:

Alexion Allocations:

Note: 1. Enter the cost percent of the allocation segments. For the majority of the lease population, this will be 100% as the lease is allocated to a single location, activity and banner. If a lease is allocated to several activities, the user will need to continue to add allocation values until the cost percent is equal to 100%.

Note 2: The Payment Company Code should be the same as the Accounting Company Code in the majority of leases in Alexion. Payment Company Code will be used for tracking appropriate company code for payment files processed by the CBRE (lease administration) team. The Accounting Company Code is the company code value that pulls into the AJD file to post in Blackline.

C.3 Enter Expenses

To add expenses, select ‘+Add’ in the top menu bar, followed by ‘Add Charges’.

Under Quick Add: Add Charges, complete the Create Charges section detail.

When account category is selected, ‘Charge Name’ is auto populated. If this is an initial expense, it should be reflecting as original term, else name should be changed in the case of a modification.

Select the vendor ‘Filler RE Vendor’ from the dropdown. This is the only vendor that is used in the AstraZeneca portfolio.

Check the Estimated checkbox if the payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.

Enter a Start Amount in the Charge Generation section.

Specify all other details, such as:

Payment Frequency - Select frequency per the lease contract.

Currency - Select from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.

Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.

Click ‘’Generate’ to generate the charge.

Review charges in the expenses schedule to confirm accuracy. Add additional charges as needed.

D) Equipment Assets: Modification

D.1 Modify Expenses

To modify charges, navigate to the Expense page on the lease record.

Select the ellipsis icon next to the charge you need to modify. Select Edit.

Make necessary modifications to the amount, account, notes or other detail associated with the charge.

Click ‘Save’.

Note: To delete a charge, select the ellipsis icon to the right of the given charge line, followed by ‘Delete’.

E) Remeasuring an Accounting Schedule

A remeasurement event occurs due to any change to the lease agreement that requires a revaluation of the right-of-use asset. Examples include a lease renewal (extension), lease termination or modification of fixed charges.

1) In the Accounting Summary section of the Accounting page of a lease, select the ellipsis icon next to the schedule you wish to remeasure. A pop-up menu is displayed showing the available types of remeasurement.

2) Select the appropriate listed remeasurement.

3) Should the remeasurement effective date impact an exported period, there would be a need for intervention from the Global Lease Accounting team to perform unexport/unapproved prior to remeasurement of the schedule. Refer to Appendix - IFRS16 Guide on Global Lease Accounting Team Intervention in CoStar (by scenario)

E.1 Renewal/Data Correction

A lease renewal is an extension on an expiring lease. During the renewal process, the lessor and lessee negotiate new lease terms or remove old ones. The new commencement and expiration dates must be re-defined for the amortization schedule to recalculate and revalue the asset appropriately.

Data Correction is performed when there is data correction made in the expense pertaining dates and amount

If the schedule has a workflow status of Reviewed prior to the rent schedule being modified, the status will automatically change to Open for Preparation. Once the expense is triggered.

The following are true when performing a renewal action on an existing schedule:

The new date range must begin after the first period. If the new range is before an approved period, the system will calculate a retroactive adjustment.

A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event, such as a renewal, that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the

accounting schedule and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.

The system will automatically calculate the difference in the newly calculated Present Value and the end liability balance prior to the new date range as the liability adjustment.

The Asset Adjustment will default to an amount equal to the liability adjustment; however, you can still edit the Total Asset Adjustment by updating the manual adjustment field if further modifications are needed, such as adjusting for an impaired asset. Simply input the manual asset adjustment field with the desired value before saving the amortization schedule.

Before performing a renewal, the user must add new or extend existing fixed charges on the Expense or Revenue page of the lease.

Select ‘Renewal’.

Complete the required fields as appropriate including:

Accounting Term Begin - Date of the execution letter/date the renewal was exercised

Accounting Term End - The new lease expiration date according to the terms of the renewal.

Click’ Calculate Values’

Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as the present value, adjustment amounts, or implicit rates. The amortization periods prior to the new accounting begin date will be preserved. The level expense will adjust beginning on the new accounting begin date. Notice that the adjustment amount will automatically populate with the balance from the prior period.

Click ‘Save & Close’.

Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.

E.2 Impairment

Impairment is a permanent decline in the value of an asset. This situation exists when the cash flows or other benefits generated by an asset decline, as determined through a periodic assessment. For example, the lease administrator may discover that the fair value of an asset is far less than the carrying amount. Therefore, the difference between the fair value of the asset and it carrying amount would be written off. The payment terms do not change in the case of an impairment and thus the lease liability amortization remains intact.

Impairments can be prospective or retroactive, depending on the impairment.

A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the accounting schedule, and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.

Select ‘Impairment’. The Remeasure - Impairment page is displayed.

Complete the following required fields as appropriate:

Accounting Term Begin - Date of the impairment.

Accounting Term End - The same Period to date as the original expiration date.

Enter a number into the Manual Asset Adjustment field. As an impairment reflects a drop in value, this should be a negative number.

Click ‘Calculate Values’.

Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as present value, adjustment amounts or implicit rates.

Click ‘Save & Close’.

Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.

E.3 Termination

When a termination event occurs, the amortization schedule needs to be updated so future payments are removed from the calculation and the remaining balance is capitalized at an accelerated pace.

The new date range typically begins the day you are notified about the termination and ends on the day of the termination. This determines how many periods by which to divide the remaining balance. Note: If the termination date falls within an exported period, Preparer should inform the Global Lease Accounting team to perform necessary action to unexport and unapprove the period prior to remeasurement of termination. For an example, assuming it is March 2023 closing, if a termination date falls within Dec 2022, preparer to move the workflow status of the lease to Open for Preparation and, inform the Global Lease Accounting team to unexport and unapprove journals from Dec 2022 to March 2023 Preparer should then be able to remeasure termination.

There are two types of termination where steps are given below:

Termination: Normal Expired

As this is a termination for a normal expired lease, a remeasurement is sufficient. Click on the ellipsis in Actions - Remeasure - Termination

2. Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule:

Accounting Term Begin - Direct Entry date. Same as per Accounting Term End.

Journal Entry Profile - IFRS16 Vehicle - Disposal (Alternatively, select ‘S4 IFRS 16 -Vehicle Disposal’, or other alternatives based on the relevant asset type for leases that should follow the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry process).

Discount Rate Profile - Select Direct Entry from the dropdown data

Annual Rate - By default should remain as 0%, as this will allow the system to calculate the gain/loss portion with the early termination date.

3. Click ‘Calculate Values’, followed by ‘Save and Close’. A termination schedule is created under Accounting Events.

Full Termination: Early Termination

1. As this is an early termination for a lease, a remeasurement is sufficient. Click on the ellipsis in Actions -

Remeasure - Full Termination

2. Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule:

Accounting Term End: Direct Entry date as Early Termination Date. By default, the Accounting Term Begin will follow the same as the Early Termination Date entered.

Journal Entry Profile: IFRS16 Vehicle - Disposal (Alternatively, select S4 IFRS 16 -Vehicle Disposal, or other alternatives based on the relevant asset type for leases that should follow the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry process). Discount Rate Profile: By default, it will auto-populate Direct Entry.

3. Click ‘Calculate Values’, followed by ‘Save and Close’. A full termination schedule is created under Accounting Events.

Check, if an additional cost allocation data is required?

If Yes, refer to Task #8.3.3.11.3: 4.7.3 Request cost allocation date update.

If no, refer to Task# 8.3.3.11.2: 4.7.2 Submit lease accounting record for approval

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Submit lease accounting record for approval
steps.detail:
Preparer will submit the lease accounting record for approval by changing the status from Open for Preparation to Prepared in CoStar. Once done, it reaches the queue of the relevant Approvers for that country/entity. This may be the Global Lease Team as a technical only activity else the Embedded Finance or Middle Office Controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

Note for Alexion:

Real estate: Alexion Controllership will approval the accounting record for all leases.

Vehicle lease: Global Lease Team will approve the accounting record as it is considered with low value impact.

Equipment lease (only applicable for BP70): Regional Controllership team will approve the accounting record.

Status gets changed to ready for approval in approval process.

Check, if errors exist.

If Yes, Repeat Task# 8.3.3.11.1: 4.7.1 Enter lease accounting records until the errors are fixed. All errors are required to be corrected in the system.

If No, Refer to Process 8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease records where the approved changes are progressed along the workflow to be reviewed.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Request cost allocation data update
steps.detail:
Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office Team raise a AZNextgen ticket to GFS Global Lease Team to request for cost allocation data update.

The GFS Global Lease Team will then refer to Process 8.3.3.16 Update lease accounting master data.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: The GFS Global Lease Team shall review the request to ensure all required information and supporting documentation are complete and accurate.
steps.detail:
GFS Lease Accounting Team reviews mass upload request via AZNextgen ticket.

This may be the Global Lease Team as a technical only activity else the Embedded Finance or Middle office controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

Check, if request meets the criteria for mass upload

If Yes, refer to process 8.3.3.15 Execute mass lease additions or modifications for guidance on the procedure that follows.

If No, refer to process 8.3.3.11.1 Enter lease accounting records where Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office must enter lease accounting details in CoStar.

activities.flowNote: Follow the approval conditions and branch instructions in each step. Rejection, rework and parallel handoffs are alternative paths, not consecutive actions.

activities.timing: Ad hoc, when lease records are added or modified.
activities.detail: Review new or modified lease records for accuracy, completeness and accounting validity before IFRS 16 period-end entries.

Appendices [3](#appendices)](#appendices) # PURPOSE The purpose of this SOP is to explain the activities required to approve and review a newly created or modified lease record, to ensure the record is accurate, complete and valid from an accounting perspective, before it is included in the period end activity that generates the relevant IFRS 16 general ledger accounting entries. The executor of an approval will depend on a country’s classification in the control environment. The GFS Global Lease team will carry out this activity as a technical step for the majority of entities. However, the largest entities (top 80% liabilities value in USD) will require a local approval. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to the below audience: - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Middle Office - Embedded Finance (local, hub) - Alexion Regional Controllership # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded: | | | |----|----| | Business Process | Description | | Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion, that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR | # # PROCEDURE ## Process Map ## Assumptions and Pre-requisites The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | |----|----| | Assumption / Pre-requisite | Description | | Pre-requisite | A contract to enter into a lease and a purchase order for that lease exists in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. | | Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. | | Assumption | All participants are familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically ‘Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)’ | | Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. | | Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. | ## Frequency This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken as additions or modifications are made to AstraZeneca / Alexion entities leased assets. ## Systems and Access The table below contains a summary of the system(s) and accesses required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | | |----|----|----| | Physical System Name | User Profile / Access Type Required | Description | | CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Lease Accounting – Workflow - Lease Approver | Required to approve a newly created or modified lease record with a status of ‘prepared’ | | CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Lease Accounting – Workflow - Lease Reviewer | Required to review a newly created or modified lease record with a status of ‘approved’ | ## Controls The table below contains a summary of the control(s) for the process this operating procedure relates to:
Control type

Control ref

 Control summary SOX/FCF Control Owner

 Review of CoStar Accounting Summary report to confirm unit’s leases are complete and accurate (review includes a check that all leases are at Workflow Approval Status = Approved or Reviewed) SOX and FCF

 CoStar is configured to enforce segregation of duties within the lease approval workflows FCF

Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.13.1

Review record for accuracy and completeness

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office/ Alexion Regional Controllership Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office/ Alexion Regional Controllership N/A N/A

In order to begin with reviewing the lease accounting records for accuracy and completeness, refer to step Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record.

Check, if the record belongs to a SOX or top 80% liabilities by USD value FCF entities?

  • If Yes, refer to below steps:

  • If No, refer to Task 8.3.3.13.2: 4.7.2 Review record for accuracy and completeness (Individual/Batch)

Individual by Lease - Review record for accuracy and completeness

  • Approver to navigate to the relevant lease reference. Click Accounting on the left navigation menu. Ensure the workflow status is Prepared prior to reviewing the lease record for accuracy and completeness. The criteria to review the accuracy and completeness is based on the description for which the lease was Open for Preparation

  • Once accuracy and completeness of lease record is reviewed, Approver to insert a comment to change the workflow status from Prepared to Approved. The comment must be specific based on the type of change (e.g.: Approved for addition/disposal/modification)

  • Click Save. The workflow status will appear as Approved.

  • The lease is ready to be reviewed.

Batch - Review record for accuracy and completeness

  • On the Accounting module, in the left navigation menu, click on Batch Change Workflow

  • The top of the page consists of the Lease Filters section, where Approver select the required selections as below:

    1. Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

    2. Classification: IFRS 16

    3. Workflow Status: Prepared

    4. Hierarchy & Country: For which the lease belongs

  • Click Apply Filters. The Leases Filtered Table at the bottom of the page displays the leases as filtered by Approver’s selections, and the Lease Filters section collapses.

  • To review the accuracy and completeness of lease record, Approver to extract the roll forward report (steps in 8.3.3.14 – Execute lease accounting reporting)

  • Once accuracy and completeness of lease record is reviewed, Approver to select the leases in the Leases Filtered Table for which to change the status. To select all leases, select the check box in header row of the left most column

  • Click Update Leases. The Update Workflow of Selected Leases dialog box displays.

  • Approver to select the New Status from the drop-down menu and enter a comment. The comment must be specific based on the number of changes and type of change (e.g.: Approved for 2 additions/2 disposals/2 modifications)

  • Click ‘Process Changes’. The Process Log Results page displays. Approver can download the resulting table to Excel by clicking the Export all data icon in the top right corner

  • Click ‘Finish’.

  • It is now ready for journal entry processing or further updates.

Check, if a record is successfully approved?

  • If Yes, then record moves to GFS Global Lease Team for review. After this review, lease accounting entries are processed. Move to task # 8.3.3.13.3: 4.7.3 Review accounting attributes

  • If No, errors are required to be corrected. Refer to Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record, activity 8.3.3.11.1.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.13.2

Review record for accuracy and completeness

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team/ Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office GFS Global Lease Team/ Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office N/A N/A

This step starts in the case of lease records belonging to non-Sox or non-top 80% liabilities by USD value FCF entity, where the GFS Global Lease Team only acts as technical support for Approver activity. The accuracy and completeness of the lease records still lies with Embedded Finance or Middle office controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

If a lease record is successfully approved, it goes to GFS Global Lease Team for review. Refer to Task# 8.3.3.13.3: 4.7.3 Review accounting attributes

If lease record is not successfully approved due to inaccuracy or incomplete lease record, refer to Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.13.3

Review accounting attributes
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

This step is where the GFS Global Lease Team performs technical review for Reviewer activity. The accuracy and completeness of the lease records still lies with Embedded Finance or Middle office controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

Referring the below steps to review accounting schedule (Individual or Batch by lease)

Individual by Lease – Review accounting attributes

  • Reviewer to navigate to the relevant the lease reference. Click ‘Accounting’ on the left navigation menu. Ensure the workflow status is Approved prior to reviewing the accounting attributes.

  • Click on Accounting Events. There are a few lines that display the accounting attributes

    • When there is an addition, there should be 1 line displayed (initial).

    • When there is a modification, there should be an additional line displayed (renewal/data correction).

    • When there is a termination, there should be an additional line displayed (termination/full termination)

  • Use Accounting Events to validate the appropriate fields:

a). Classification Type and Amortisation

b). Journal Entry Profile

c). Base Rent Begin and End Date

d). Discount Rate profile

e). Currency

f). Amortisation Amount

  • Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to insert a comment to change the workflow status from Approved to Reviewed.

  • Click ‘Save’. The workflow status will appear as Reviewed.

Batch – Review accounting attributes

  • On the Accounting module, in the left navigation menu, click on ‘Batch Change Workflow’.

  • The top of the page consists of the Lease Filters section, where Reviewer selects the required selections as below:

    • Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

    • Classification: IFRS 16

    • Workflow Status: Approved

    • Hierarchy & Country: For which the lease belongs

  • Click ‘Apply Filters’. The Leases Filtered Table at the bottom of the page displays the leases as filtered by Reviewer’s selections, and the Lease Filters section collapses.

  • To review the accounting attributes, Reviewer to extract the roll forward report (steps in 8.3.3.14 – Execute lease accounting reporting). For example, review the following:

    • Journal entry Profile

    • End Date

    • Cost Center / Internal Order

  • Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to select the leases in the Leases Filtered Table for which to change the status. To select all leases, select the check box in header row of the leftmost column.

  • Click ‘Update Leases’. The Update Workflow of Selected Leases dialog box displays.

  • Reviewer to select the ‘New Status’ from the drop-down menu and enter a comment.

  • Click ‘Process Changes’. The Process Log Results page displays. Reviewer can download the resulting table to Excel by clicking the Export all data icon in the top right corner.

  • Click ‘Finish’.

steps.title: Review record for accuracy and completeness
steps.detail:
In order to begin with reviewing the lease accounting records for accuracy and completeness, refer to step Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record.

Check, if the record belongs to a SOX or top 80% liabilities by USD value FCF entities?

If Yes, refer to below steps:

If No, refer to Task 8.3.3.13.2: 4.7.2 Review record for accuracy and completeness (Individual/Batch)

Individual by Lease - Review record for accuracy and completeness

Approver to navigate to the relevant lease reference. Click Accounting on the left navigation menu. Ensure the workflow status is Prepared prior to reviewing the lease record for accuracy and completeness. The criteria to review the accuracy and completeness is based on the description for which the lease was Open for Preparation

Once accuracy and completeness of lease record is reviewed, Approver to insert a comment to change the workflow status from Prepared to Approved. The comment must be specific based on the type of change (e.g.: Approved for addition/disposal/modification)

Click Save. The workflow status will appear as Approved.

The lease is ready to be reviewed.

Batch - Review record for accuracy and completeness

On the Accounting module, in the left navigation menu, click on Batch Change Workflow

The top of the page consists of the Lease Filters section, where Approver select the required selections as below:

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Classification: IFRS 16

Workflow Status: Prepared

Hierarchy & Country: For which the lease belongs

Click Apply Filters. The Leases Filtered Table at the bottom of the page displays the leases as filtered by Approver’s selections, and the Lease Filters section collapses.

To review the accuracy and completeness of lease record, Approver to extract the roll forward report (steps in 8.3.3.14 - Execute lease accounting reporting)

Once accuracy and completeness of lease record is reviewed, Approver to select the leases in the Leases Filtered Table for which to change the status. To select all leases, select the check box in header row of the left most column

Click Update Leases. The Update Workflow of Selected Leases dialog box displays.

Approver to select the New Status from the drop-down menu and enter a comment. The comment must be specific based on the number of changes and type of change (e.g.: Approved for 2 additions/2 disposals/2 modifications)

Click ‘Process Changes’. The Process Log Results page displays. Approver can download the resulting table to Excel by clicking the Export all data icon in the top right corner

Click ‘Finish’.

It is now ready for journal entry processing or further updates.

Check, if a record is successfully approved?

If Yes, then record moves to GFS Global Lease Team for review. After this review, lease accounting entries are processed. Move to task # 8.3.3.13.3: 4.7.3 Review accounting attributes

If No, errors are required to be corrected. Refer to Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record, activity 8.3.3.11.1.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Review record for accuracy and completeness
steps.detail:
This step starts in the case of lease records belonging to non-Sox or non-top 80% liabilities by USD value FCF entity, where the GFS Global Lease Team only acts as technical support for Approver activity. The accuracy and completeness of the lease records still lies with Embedded Finance or Middle office controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

If a lease record is successfully approved, it goes to GFS Global Lease Team for review. Refer to Task# 8.3.3.13.3: 4.7.3 Review accounting attributes

If lease record is not successfully approved due to inaccuracy or incomplete lease record, refer to Process 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Review accounting attributes
steps.detail:
This step is where the GFS Global Lease Team performs technical review for Reviewer activity. The accuracy and completeness of the lease records still lies with Embedded Finance or Middle office controllers as dictated by the SOX/FCF controls.

Referring the below steps to review accounting schedule (Individual or Batch by lease)

Individual by Lease - Review accounting attributes

Reviewer to navigate to the relevant the lease reference. Click ‘Accounting’ on the left navigation menu. Ensure the workflow status is Approved prior to reviewing the accounting attributes.

Click on Accounting Events. There are a few lines that display the accounting attributes

When there is an addition, there should be 1 line displayed (initial).

When there is a modification, there should be an additional line displayed (renewal/data correction).

When there is a termination, there should be an additional line displayed (termination/full termination)

Use Accounting Events to validate the appropriate fields:

a). Classification Type and Amortisation

b). Journal Entry Profile

c). Base Rent Begin and End Date

d). Discount Rate profile

e). Currency

f). Amortisation Amount

Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to insert a comment to change the workflow status from Approved to Reviewed.

Click ‘Save’. The workflow status will appear as Reviewed.

Batch - Review accounting attributes

On the Accounting module, in the left navigation menu, click on ‘Batch Change Workflow’.

The top of the page consists of the Lease Filters section, where Reviewer selects the required selections as below:

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Classification: IFRS 16

Workflow Status: Approved

Hierarchy & Country: For which the lease belongs

Click ‘Apply Filters’. The Leases Filtered Table at the bottom of the page displays the leases as filtered by Reviewer’s selections, and the Lease Filters section collapses.

To review the accounting attributes, Reviewer to extract the roll forward report (steps in 8.3.3.14 - Execute lease accounting reporting). For example, review the following:

Journal entry Profile

End Date

Cost Center / Internal Order

Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to select the leases in the Leases Filtered Table for which to change the status. To select all leases, select the check box in header row of the leftmost column.

Click ‘Update Leases’. The Update Workflow of Selected Leases dialog box displays.

Reviewer to select the ‘New Status’ from the drop-down menu and enter a comment.

Click ‘Process Changes’. The Process Log Results page displays. Reviewer can download the resulting table to Excel by clicking the Export all data icon in the top right corner.

Click ‘Finish’.

activities.flowNote: Follow the approval conditions and branch instructions in each step. Rejection, rework and parallel handoffs are alternative paths, not consecutive actions.

8.3.3.14.2

Create and Modify report as required
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
Licensed CoStar Users Licensed CoStar Users N/A N/A

Below outlines the steps for the creation and modification ad-hoc reports.

Create an Ad Hoc report.

  1. Navigate to the Reports module.

  1. Click ‘Create Report’ in the top right.

  1. Type a name for the report and select the format (Excel or PDF).

  1. Select the data set to use for the report. The naming of the data sets is fairly intuitive. For example, if you are creating a report for lease options, you can type ‘Options’ into the Select Data Set search and the data sets related to options will appear. Some commonly used data sets include:

  1. Lease Summary – key dates and most data fields from the building and lease abstract.

  1. GL Event Summary – Pull expense related data

  1. Lease Allocations – Pull Location, Activity and Banner data with lease data

  1. Lease Accounting – Raw data of accounting schedules

  1. Determine if the report should return Active, Archived or Both records.

  1. Select the fields you would like to pull into the report. You can search by field name or scroll through the list. Double click or click and drag a field to the ‘Selected Fields’ section to add it to the report.

  1. Click ‘Criteria’ to add parameters around the data pulling into the report. The user can select a field, like Commencement Date, then determine the criteria for the data field such as greater than today’s date.

  1. If a user has access to both the AstraZeneca and Alexion portfolios (E.g., Master Data Administration Team), remember to filter for the relevant portfolio using the Criteria ‘Portfolio’ Equals ‘Alexion’.

  1. Click ‘Run Report’ to view your report based on the selected fields and criteria. If this report is one that you will run more than once, you can save the report by clicking ‘Save’. To save the report to your Favourites List, click the star next to the Name and Type towards the top of the page.

  1. Select ‘Close’. If you saved the report, you could search for it again under the Report Name field in the Reports module.

  1. To share the report with other users, right click the report name and click ‘Share’. Select ‘Add New’ and specify the user/group and rights you will assign to that person/group.

Below are details to schedule an Ad Hoc Report

  1. To schedule the report to be emailed to you on a periodic basis, right click the report name and click ‘Schedule’.

  2. Specify the parameters related to the scheduling of the report including a name for the schedule, frequency of report generation, the begin and end dates of the schedule and the delivery list. You can specify CoStar or non-CoStar users in the email distribution.

  3. Click Save.

In the event a report requires modifications follow the below steps:

  1. Find the relevant report and click on the ellipsis (three dots to the right side of the specific report) you wish to modify followed by clicking ’Edit’.

  1. Now change the selected field(s) as per your required modifications such as Portfolio ID, Account ID, Account Name code, Number and/ or other appropriate fields.

3. Once all changes are done, click on ‘Save’ so the modifications are saved.

There are common Ad Hoc data sets and Data fields in the reports in CoStar

Common Ad Hoc Data Sets

• Lease Summary – Includes all fields from Center, Store and Lease abstracts

• GL Event Summary – Includes ‘GL’ fields for expense/revenue charge schedule such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes

• GL Exported Transactions – Transaction history log, includes ‘GL’ fields for all exported expense/revenue charges such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes

• Lease Accounting by Period with Allocations– Includes accounting schedule inputs and balances by period

Common Ad Hoc Data Fields

Generally, the field names in the ad hoc data sets are aligned with the naming convention of the field on the lease abstract. The following fields are calculated fields in the data sets that are useful for reporting.

• Current Term Remaining – Calculates from today’s date to current lease expiration date

• Current Annual Rent – Calculates annual rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent

• Current Month Expenses – Calculates sum of total monthly rent and non-rent charges

• Current Month Rent Expenses – Calculates sum of monthly rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent

• Remaining Renewal Options – Defines number of renewal options that are Active

• Next Option Date/s – Defines critical dates associated with next available option such as Option Begin Date, Option End Date and Option Notification Start Date

See below steps to execute specific reports with required parameters.

Accounting Roll-Forward Report

  1. Navigate to the Reports module.

  1. Find the Accounting Roll-Forward report by searching in the Report Name field or scrolling down the list. Select the name of the report or green play icon under Actions to run the report.

  1. A new window will appear. Select the parameters as they relate to the configurations of

the schedules you would like to include in the report. Remember to select the appropriate portfolio (AstraZeneca / Alexion).

  1. Portfolio – Select AstraZeneca / Alexion

  2. Country (Note: The report is country specific not company code specific. Hence upon downloading the report, to view company code specific leases, filter by Client Lease ID)

  3. Include Allocations – Whether or not allocations should be included as a part of the report. Select ‘Yes’ to include Location, Activity and Banner related data points.

  4. Period From

  5. Period To

  6. The rest of the parameters are auto populated, to validate prior to viewing the report.

  1. Once the parameters are specified, click ‘View Report’.

  1. After CoStar has emailed the report link, click on the link to download the report.
