steps.title: Document request and submit to CoStar user
steps.detail:
This task starts when non-license holders (i.e. users who cannot access CoStar) request a Lease accounting related report via AZNextgen /Outlook to from a Licensed CoStar User

Once requested, CoStar users to check if relevant report already exist or not.

If yes, move to task 8.3.3.14.4 4.7.4 Execute report with required parameters.

If No, refer to step 8.3.3.14.2 4.7.2 Create and modify the report as required.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Create and Modify report as required
steps.detail:
Below outlines the steps for the creation and modification ad-hoc reports.

Create an Ad Hoc report.

Navigate to the Reports module.

Click ‘Create Report’ in the top right.

Type a name for the report and select the format (Excel or PDF).

Select the data set to use for the report. The naming of the data sets is fairly intuitive. For example, if you are creating a report for lease options, you can type ‘Options’ into the Select Data Set search and the data sets related to options will appear. Some commonly used data sets include:

Lease Summary - key dates and most data fields from the building and lease abstract.

GL Event Summary - Pull expense related data

Lease Allocations - Pull Location, Activity and Banner data with lease data

Lease Accounting - Raw data of accounting schedules

Determine if the report should return Active, Archived or Both records.

Select the fields you would like to pull into the report. You can search by field name or scroll through the list. Double click or click and drag a field to the ‘Selected Fields’ section to add it to the report.

Click ‘Criteria’ to add parameters around the data pulling into the report. The user can select a field, like Commencement Date, then determine the criteria for the data field such as greater than today’s date.

If a user has access to both the AstraZeneca and Alexion portfolios (E.g., Master Data Administration Team), remember to filter for the relevant portfolio using the Criteria ‘Portfolio’ Equals ‘Alexion’.

Click ‘Run Report’ to view your report based on the selected fields and criteria. If this report is one that you will run more than once, you can save the report by clicking ‘Save’. To save the report to your Favourites List, click the star next to the Name and Type towards the top of the page.

Select ‘Close’. If you saved the report, you could search for it again under the Report Name field in the Reports module.

To share the report with other users, right click the report name and click ‘Share’. Select ‘Add New’ and specify the user/group and rights you will assign to that person/group.

Below are details to schedule an Ad Hoc Report

To schedule the report to be emailed to you on a periodic basis, right click the report name and click ‘Schedule’.

Specify the parameters related to the scheduling of the report including a name for the schedule, frequency of report generation, the begin and end dates of the schedule and the delivery list. You can specify CoStar or non-CoStar users in the email distribution.

Click Save.

In the event a report requires modifications follow the below steps:

Find the relevant report and click on the ellipsis (three dots to the right side of the specific report) you wish to modify followed by clicking ’Edit’.

Now change the selected field(s) as per your required modifications such as Portfolio ID, Account ID, Account Name code, Number and/ or other appropriate fields.

3. Once all changes are done, click on ‘Save’ so the modifications are saved.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Test and reconcile report
steps.detail:
Once the relevant report is created and saved in CoStar or relevant modifications have been made, follow the steps to test and reconcile the report:

Navigate to the Reports module.

Search under the Report Name field in the Reports module.

Check if the report is accurate and complete

If Yes, move to Step 8.3.3.14.4 4.7.4 Execute report with required parameters

If No, move to step 8.3.3.14.2 4.7.2 Create or Modify report as required.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Execute report with required parameters
steps.detail:
There are common Ad Hoc data sets and Data fields in the reports in CoStar

Common Ad Hoc Data Sets

Lease Summary - Includes all fields from Center, Store and Lease abstracts

GL Event Summary - Includes ‘GL’ fields for expense/revenue charge schedule such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes

GL Exported Transactions - Transaction history log, includes ‘GL’ fields for all exported expense/revenue charges such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes

Lease Accounting by Period with Allocations- Includes accounting schedule inputs and balances by period

Common Ad Hoc Data Fields

Generally, the field names in the ad hoc data sets are aligned with the naming convention of the field on the lease abstract. The following fields are calculated fields in the data sets that are useful for reporting.

Current Term Remaining - Calculates from today’s date to current lease expiration date

Current Annual Rent - Calculates annual rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent

Current Month Expenses - Calculates sum of total monthly rent and non-rent charges

Current Month Rent Expenses - Calculates sum of monthly rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent

Remaining Renewal Options - Defines number of renewal options that are Active

Next Option Date/s - Defines critical dates associated with next available option such as Option Begin Date, Option End Date and Option Notification Start Date

See below steps to execute specific reports with required parameters.

Accounting Roll-Forward Report

Navigate to the Reports module.

Find the Accounting Roll-Forward report by searching in the Report Name field or scrolling down the list. Select the name of the report or green play icon under Actions to run the report.

A new window will appear. Select the parameters as they relate to the configurations of

the schedules you would like to include in the report. Remember to select the appropriate portfolio (AstraZeneca / Alexion).

Portfolio - Select AstraZeneca / Alexion

Country (Note: The report is country specific not company code specific. Hence upon downloading the report, to view company code specific leases, filter by Client Lease ID)

Include Allocations - Whether or not allocations should be included as a part of the report. Select ‘Yes’ to include Location, Activity and Banner related data points.

Period From

Period To

The rest of the parameters are auto populated, to validate prior to viewing the report.

Once the parameters are specified, click ‘View Report’.

After CoStar has emailed the report link, click on the link to download the report.

Accounting Summary Report

Navigate to the Reports module.

Find the Accounting Summary report by searching in the Report Name field or scrolling down the list. Select the name of the report or green play icon under Actions to run the report.

A new window will appear. Select the parameters as they relate to the configurations of the schedules you would like to include in the report.

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Include Allocation: Yes

System Lease Status: Active

Classification: IFRS16

Country: (Choose the country that is required)

Period: Jan 2025

Periods out: 12

Delivery method: Email me a report link (can choose to generate through browser, or to email the link once report is ready. It is recommended to choose ‘Email the report link’ delivery method if the lease database is huge)

Note: Leave the remaining fields unchanged, as they are already set to their default values

Once the parameters are specified, click ‘View Report’.

After CoStar has emailed the report link, click on the link to download the report.

Accounting IFRS16 Disclosure Report

Navigate to the Reports module.

Find the Accounting IFRS16 Disclosure report by searching in the Report Name field or scrolling down the list. Select the name of the report or green play icon under Actions to run the report.

A new window will appear. Select the parameters as they relate to the configurations of the schedules you would like to include in the report.

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Include allocation: True

System Lease Status: Active

Allocation Segment 1: Select All

Reporting Year: Current Year

Reporting Period: Current Quarter

Include Detail Support: Do Not Include Details

Delivery method: Email me a report link (can choose to generate through browser, or to email the link once report is ready)

Note: FX rates (Average and Spot) show on the Exchange Rates tab

Once the parameters are specified, click ‘View Report’.

After CoStar has emailed the report link, click on the link to download the report.

Discount Rate Validation report

No parameters need to be chosen

Double click on report and it auto runs and downloads to Excel

All discount factors (entire history) are downloaded

Accounting Forecast Report

For Financial Report Compilation (Treasury)

Go to reporting modules (Reports)

Type Accounting Forecast in the search box

Click and a pop out window will come out to choose the desired criteria.

Choose criteria accordingly

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Include allocation: Yes

System Lease Status: Active

Classification: IFRS16

Country: All

Period: Jan 2023 (choose start period you’re looking for)

Periods out: +6 Fiscal year

Forecast Type: Liability

Delivery method: Email me a report link (can choose to generate through browser, or to email the link once report is ready)

Once report is ready, choose to save in Excel

Repeat the same steps.

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Include allocation: Yes

System Lease Status: Active

Classification: IFRS16

Country: All

Period: Jan 2029 (since CoStar can only give up to 6 years, to obtain for 10 years would need to choose period of Jan 2029 which is 6 years after Jan 2023)

Periods out: +6 Fiscal year

Forecast Type: Liability

Delivery method: Email me a report link (can choose to generate through browser, or to email the link once report is ready)

These two files would need to be combined in one file to give 10 years of liability balance for treasury reporting.

For General Use

Go to the reporting module (Reports).

Type Accounting Forecast in the search box

Click and pop out window will come out to choose the desired criteria

Choose criteria accordingly

Compulsory field

Portfolio: AstraZeneca / Alexion

Include allocation: Yes

System Lease Status: Active

Classification: IFRS16

Field to choose according to country/period/accounting impact

Country: Argentina

(choose country you required information on)

Period: Jan 2023 (choose start period you’re looking for)

Periods out: 72 months (choose according to until which period you’re looking information for, number of months will give monthly number, fiscal year will group the data yearly)

Forecast Type: Asset Balance, Asset Amortization, Liability Interest Expense, Payment, Short Term Liability or Long-Term Liability

(Choose according to what accounting information you’re looking for, above is the common field)

Delivery method: Email me a report link (can choose to generate through browser, or to email the link once report is ready)

Once report is ready, choose to save in Excel

ERH Report

Navigate to the Reports module.

Find the ERH Source Report by searching in the Report Name field or scrolling down the list. Select the name of the report or green play icon under Actions to edit the report.

A new window will appear. Select criteria and edit the criteria as they relate to the configurations of the schedules you would like to include in the report. Click Run Report.

Criteria

Tenant Legal Name: Company Code

Exported Date: The date in which journals were exported

Report will be downloaded in Excel File.

Once report is executed, does this report to distributed?

If yes, follow the step 8.3.3.14.5 4.7.5 Extract the report and distribution

If No, task is completed, and no further action is needed

steps.title: Extract the report and distribution
steps.detail:
User extract report and distributes as per the request received. Follow the step below to execute this task.

Select the export icon to reveal the available export formats. Select the desired format and the file will export to your hard drive.

After extraction of the report, share it to the distributor via Outlook or AZNextgen.

Appendices [3](#appendices)](#appendices) # # PURPOSE The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to either create new records or modify existing records using the mass processing (ETL) tool in the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. These activities can differ depending on the asset class (property, vehicles or other) but will only ever be executed by the GFS Global Lease Team. This process is considered highly complex and should not be undertaken unless the volume qualifications documented in the AZ Global Lease Accounting Standard are met at a minimum. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Middle Office - Embedded Finance (local, hub) - Alexion Regional Controllership # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded: | | | |----|----| | Business Process | Description | | Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR | # # PROCEDURE ## Process Maps ## 4.2 Assumptions and Prerequisites The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | |----|----| | Assumption / Prerequisite | Description | | Pre-requisite | A contract to enter a lease and a purchase order for that lease exists in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. | | Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. | | Pre-requisite | A qualifying request exists to trigger the mass upload process. | | Assumption | All participants are familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically ‘Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)’ | | Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. | | Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. | ## Frequency This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken as additions or modifications are made to an AstraZeneca or Alexion entities leased assets ## Systems and Access The table below contains a summary of the system(s) and accesses required for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | | |----|----|----| | Physical System Name | User Profile / Access Type Required | Description | | CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Lease Accounting | Required to add or modify mass lease accounting record. Restricted by entity. | | AZNextgen | R2R messaging | The standard mechanism to engage with the GFS Global Lease team. | ## Controls The table below contains a summary of the control(s) for the process this operating procedure relates to: | **Control type** | **Control ref** | **Control summary** | **SOX/FCF** | **Control Owner** | |----|----|----|----|----| | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | ## Metrics The table below contains a summary of the metrics / measures for the process this operating procedure relates to: | | | | | | |----|----|----|----|----| | Metric Id / Name | Metric Type | Metric Description | Metric Owner | Target Value / Output | | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | ## Process Detail The following step by step instructions explain how to perform the work involved in the process:
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.15.1

Download, complete and send Data Collection Template

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed

AstraZeneca: Embedded Finance/ GFS Middle Office

The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system. The mass upload DCT will be maintained by GFS Global Lease Team on every WD+5 and available in Nucleus Page for download.

The process starts from task 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record. If a market meets the mass upload criteria, refer step below:

Note: 3rd party vehicle lease data sent directly to KL team will come through email and it is highly recommended for GFS Global Lease Team to analyse the data using the mass upload DCT prior to uploading the changes in CoStar via ETL templates.

Note for Alexion Japan vehicle leases: Japan Controllership team will translate the Vehicle lease report received from Orix and provide it to GFS Global Lease Team via BOX location on 11th of the month. It is highly recommended for GFS Global Lease Team to analyse the data using the mass upload DCT prior to uploading the changes in CoStar via ETL templates.

It is highly recommended for GFS Global Lease Team to analyse the data using the mass upload DCT prior to uploading the changes in CoStar via ETL templates

Note for Alexion UK, Austria, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Switzerland, Turkey: Local Finance Markets to download the mass upload Data Collection Template from Nucleus Page, complete and send the completed form via AZNextgen to GFS Global Lease Team (applicable only in case of more than 30 updates per month/country).

AZ Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office to download the mass upload Data Collection Template from Nucleus Page, complete and send the completed form via AZNextgen to GFS Global Lease Team.

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team Embedded Finance/ GFS Middle Office Embedded Finance/ GFS Middle Office
When there are multiple creation and modification of lease accounting record required, Mass creation or modification to be executed. GFS Global Lease Team require consulting with in-country finance to confirm mass upload DCT attribute (quality and characteristic) and Communication channel is AZNextgen in stakeholder, which can be used to import the data in one go rather than doing one by one.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.15.3

Populate ETL templates with required attributes and review
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

Navigate to the Admin module, click ETL

Filter AZ in the Import Template Name, select the respective template available (refer appendix for available templates in AZ). Populate the ETL templates for respective fields based on information available in mass upload DCT. If preparation is completed, refer steps in Task # 8.3.3.15.4 Upload ETL templates to CoStar
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.15.4 4.6.4 Upload ETL templates to CoStar
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

Once a template has been populated with all the desired data, Navigate to the ETL tool.

Select Import Data at the top left-hand corner of the screen

This will take the user to the ETL import wizard. Select the Choose File button and find the populated template you wish to upload into the application

Once a template is selected, the tool will populate the information about the template so the user can confirm the details of the file that was selected. The user should confirm the File Name is correct, the Portfolio is correct, and the Import Template Name matches the desired ETL type. If the details match expectations, select Next

The tool will then go through the validation process, confirming if the data in the template is in the appropriate format for upload. During this process, the tool will also tell the end user how many records the application will insert and how many records the application will update.

  • A record that is being inserted signifies that there are no other records of this type with a matching key field (Source Import ID). The application will create new records for these line items.

  • A record that is being updated signifies that there are records of this type with matching key field (Source Import ID), so the tool will replace all associated data in the application with the data in the template.

  • It is the user’s responsibility to confirm these metrics are accurate and that the data should be inserted or updated as this screen suggests

As template import the data in ETL, sometimes there is validation error and warning shown. It is due to incorrect fields were selected and showing in Field Name, Row Number and source data table. So, to avoid the error, Select correct field in template and import again with appropriable template until validation get successfully.

Once the data has been successfully validated by the application, select the Continue button to move on to the final stage of the ETL loading process

The application will show for a final time the number of records that will be inserted and updated as well as the number of records that are invalid and will be skipped. If all this information looks correct, select Process Valid Records to begin loading the data.

The tool will then take the user back to the Imports screen, where the template that was just validated will be in a Queued status. This means the template is waiting to be uploaded but has not begun loading yet.

The Status will update to In Progress once the template begins loading to the application.

The Status will update to Completed once the template has been successfully loaded into the application. The Records Processed column shows how many records were successfully loaded.

Check if the addition or modification is successfully mass uploaded?

In the case of yes, Move to Step 8.3.3.15.5 4.6.5 Inform in Country requestor via AZNextgen

In case of No, check if Master data require to update?

If Yes, Move to step 8.3.3.16 Update lease accounting master data.

If No, move back to follow step 8.3.3.15.2. 4.6.2 Consult with In-country finance to confirm template attributes.

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed

Once GFS Global Lease Team has uploaded template in ETL tool and this is successfully loaded, need to communicate to In-country requestor for the same via AZNextgen.

After informed to stakeholder, Follow the task 8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease accounting entries

steps.title: Upload ETL templates to CoStar
steps.detail:
Once a template has been populated with all the desired data, Navigate to the ETL tool.

Select Import Data at the top left-hand corner of the screen

This will take the user to the ETL import wizard. Select the Choose File button and find the populated template you wish to upload into the application

Once a template is selected, the tool will populate the information about the template so the user can confirm the details of the file that was selected. The user should confirm the File Name is correct, the Portfolio is correct, and the Import Template Name matches the desired ETL type. If the details match expectations, select Next

The tool will then go through the validation process, confirming if the data in the template is in the appropriate format for upload. During this process, the tool will also tell the end user how many records the application will insert and how many records the application will update.

A record that is being inserted signifies that there are no other records of this type with a matching key field (Source Import ID). The application will create new records for these line items.

A record that is being updated signifies that there are records of this type with matching key field (Source Import ID), so the tool will replace all associated data in the application with the data in the template.

It is the user’s responsibility to confirm these metrics are accurate and that the data should be inserted or updated as this screen suggests

As template import the data in ETL, sometimes there is validation error and warning shown. It is due to incorrect fields were selected and showing in Field Name, Row Number and source data table. So, to avoid the error, Select correct field in template and import again with appropriable template until validation get successfully.

Once the data has been successfully validated by the application, select the Continue button to move on to the final stage of the ETL loading process

The application will show for a final time the number of records that will be inserted and updated as well as the number of records that are invalid and will be skipped. If all this information looks correct, select Process Valid Records to begin loading the data.

The tool will then take the user back to the Imports screen, where the template that was just validated will be in a Queued status. This means the template is waiting to be uploaded but has not begun loading yet.

The Status will update to In Progress once the template begins loading to the application.

The Status will update to Completed once the template has been successfully loaded into the application. The Records Processed column shows how many records were successfully loaded.

Check if the addition or modification is successfully mass uploaded?

In the case of yes, Move to Step 8.3.3.15.5 4.6.5 Inform in Country requestor via AZNextgen

In case of No, check if Master data require to update?

If Yes, Move to step 8.3.3.16 Update lease accounting master data.

If No, move back to follow step 8.3.3.15.2. 4.6.2 Consult with In-country finance to confirm template attributes.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.detail:
Once GFS Global Lease Team has uploaded template in ETL tool and this is successfully loaded, need to communicate to In-country requestor for the same via AZNextgen.

After informed to stakeholder, Follow the task 8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease accounting entries

This SOP advises of the necessary steps to take should this be the case. # AUDIENCE This SOP applies to - GFS Global Lease Team - GFS Middle Office - Embedded Finance (local, hub) - Alexion Regional Controllership # SCOPE The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to.   • Center – WBS – WBS Name

  • Code – Company Code

  • Number – WBS

  • Center – Product Brand - Product Brand Name

  • Code - Product Brand

  • Number - Product Brand

  • Segment - Select Product Brand from the dropdown

Filter the segment field as per the requirement (e.g., CC, Code, Number).

Once segment is filtered, click on the yellow pencil box located at the right side section. Make necessary updates to the segment (e.g., see cost center example above) and then click on the save button. This is how master data is updated and information will be reflected

steps.detail:
Once the update in master data has been done in lease accounting record, the GFS Global Lease Team to send confirmation to update and close the ticket.

Moving forward, two scenarios are captured below to inform potential further necessary steps to be completed by the the respective parties

Is a lease accounting creation or modification pending?

If yes, move to task 8.3.3.11 Create or modify a lease accounting record

If No, Task is completed, no more action needed.

Is there any mass update pending in lease accounting?

If yes, Move to step 8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease records

If No, Task is completed, no more action needed.

Review Lease Alerts page

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed

In this process, check accounting workflow is filtered by “Prepared” and “Approved” to ensure:

  • Any modifications added due to any reason have been reviewed before processing lease accounting monthly entries

In the Accounting module, select “Lease Alerts” to view the lease alerts by severity or another criterion. This view is overall for the entire portfolio you have access to.

If you have access to both the AstraZeneca and Alexion portfolios, use the Portfolio filter at the top of the page to select the relevant portfolio you would like to filter for.

To view lease alerts by individual lease, at the top right page of the Abstract, Accounting, Expenses, and/or Revenue pages for that lease, an alerts button will display with the number of alerts in parentheses and the text displaying in accordance with the colour of the most severe alert.

Click the button to display the Lease Alerts pop-up window to process the alerts. After closing out, navigate back to the Lease Alerts page using the breadcrumb trail at the top left of the page.

Remediate Alerts
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

  • Select the check box next to each line item you would like to approve. If you would like to check all line items, select the check box next to the column headers to do so.

  1. Select ‘Download’ to create an Excel worksheet with the journal entries lines for leases that met the filtered criteria.

  1. Next >>”.

This process applies to all leases for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR, with the exception of the leases which have cutover to SAP S/4HANA during the ongoing staged rollouts to the Axial S/4HANA integration, replacing the Blackline journal entry processing process.

Following completion of the staged rollout across all entities to the Axial S/4HANA integration, the Blackline journal entry from CoStar processing only will become redundant. Blackline will still be used for reconciliations and manual adjustment requirements.

Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.18.1

Transmit lease accounting entries

Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Global Lease Team GFS Global Lease Team N/A N/A

The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system

This process starts from Task# 8.3.3.17: 4.7.1 Process lease accounting entries.

Reversing Journal Entry Status (Un-export & Un-approve)

When the journal entry for a lease has been approved and exported within CoStar, the JE Status column in the accounting schedule will change from Scheduled to Approved to Exported.

Once the status is marked as ‘Exported’, the lease will no longer appear in the Journal Entry to Approve or Journal Entry to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to prevent re-processing of the journal entry. In the event if the user needs to modify an accounting schedule after journal entries have been exported, they will need to go through the following steps to revert the JE Status back to ‘Scheduled’. The user can make modifications for a period when it’s in ‘Scheduled’ status, then will go through the Journal Entries to Approve and Journal Entries to Export steps again for this lease.

1) Navigate to the lease record by using the quick search or list pages in the Portfolio module.

2) Navigate to the Accounting page.

3) On the accounting schedule, locate the JE Status for the period that needs to be reversed. Click ‘Exported’.

4) In the pop up, review the journal entry that has been exported. Select ‘unexport’.

5) After the system has unexported the journal, select unapprove.

6) The pop up should now display Preview Journal Entry. Select ‘Close’.

7) Ensure the JE Status for the period is now marked as Scheduled before making any changes to the lease record.

Changes can be made to expenses, allocations or other information that should have been updated before processing the journal entry. Navigate to Journal Entries to Approve,Journal Entries to Export, or AstraZeneca/Alexion JE Export reports to reprocess the journal entry for the period. If more than one lease should be reversed, follow the steps for Offline Reversal for Journal Entry.

Offline Reversals for Journal Entries

Journal entry reversal occurs via an offline report located in the Reports module. The report is called Offline Reverse Journal Entry. Journal entries follow a 2-step process of approval and export, and both the unexport and unapprove can be accommodated in the Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

1) Navigate to the Reports module.

2) Search for ‘Offline reverse’.

3) Select Offline Reverse Journal Entry report.

4) Complete the criteria listed below as needed to filter the file for the appropriate journal entries that need to be reversed.

• Hierarchy

• Period From

• Period To

• Classification Type

• Amortization Profile

• Journal Entry Profile

• Journal Entry Status*

• Currency

• Workflow Status

• Country

• System Export Batch ID

• Client Batch Number

*Note - The filter for Journal Entry Status has the biggest impact on the content of the report. One must select either Approved or Exported as the status.

5) Based the selection of filters, the system will generate an Excel file to complete.

6) Open the Excel file and find the Actions column. Available Actions in the report for each journal entry will vary as follows:

• If Journal Entry Status was Approved – Actions: unapprove, Skip

• If Journal Entry Status was Exported – Actions: unexport, unexport & unapprove, Skip

7) Review each row and make an update to the Action column, indicating what action to take for each lease.

8) Save the Excel file.

9) Navigate to the Reports module.

10) Upload the Excel file by clicking the Upload Offline Template and following the prompts. It may take up to 15 minutes to complete the processing once the file has been uploaded.

Note: In the event unexport/unapproved action is performed in CoStar, a reversal journal should be manually prepared to post in Blackline. This process should undergo the normal journal posting in Blackline as per Blackline policy.

8.3.3.18.2

Build lease accounting journals
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Business Administrator GFS Business Administrator N/A N/A

Once the sFTP file is transmitted to the lease accounting journal, it will send to the Blackline tool via global scape for producing of the JE template.

After it has been sent to the Blackline tool, the Lease accounting journal is prepared in the BL template and Blackline admin will process the automated journal entry on WD-1, It leads to follow two processes as per scenarios.

  • If all fields in the template are correctly validated in Blackline and there are no errors, the posting has been successfully completed. Follow task 8.3.2.24. Process Automated Journal Entries where the impact will be documented in the SAP lease accounting books.

  • If any errors are encountered (E.g. Cost Centre is blocked, Internal Order does not exist etc., the workflow will automatically be assigned to a member of the Global Lease team for manual remediation. Once updated detail is received and updated in the BL template the manual JE can be processed with the impact shown in the Lease account in SAP books.

  1. Status will remain as Not Prepared

  1. Entry will be required to be updated to resolve the errors and select Validate and Certify.

  • Once the month end lease entry is posted in SAP, this process is completed.

Business Business N/A Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office

Business initiates the request for creation of Intangible Asset Interco Transfer to Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office by providing the Legal Contract or AIN document.

AIN document is only applicable to deal value more than USD10 million.

Sample email which is from Project Moon on November 2022 is given below:

Business is required to provide some guidance from AIN or Legal document to Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office on information required for Transferor (Selling Entity) and Transferee (Buying Entity).

Transferor (Selling Entity)

  1. Asset to be transferred is relating to which existing Intangible Asset (IP License)

  2. The amount of the deal that reflect as gross to be transferred (ie Cost and Accumulated Depreciation)

  3. Expected exchange currency to be used if the local entity currency is not in USD

  4. Date of disposal or retirement of the assets

  5. The remaining useful life

  6. Cost Centre to be used

Transferee (Buying Entity)

  1. Whether this is a new project or addition milestone

  2. The gross amount to be received and as capitalised as Cost with Accumulated Depreciation

  3. Expected exchange currency to be used if the local entity currency is not in USD

  4. Date of acquisition

  5. If the asset required amortisation. If yes, how long would be the expected useful life.

  6. The date of the project would end whether this requires a revised.

  7. Cost Centre to be used

From selling entity perspective, two steps are needed:

  1. Retire the assets retirement by referring to 4.7.2 Intangible Asset Disposal or Retirement. The asset of selling party will be retired from the FA register to gain / loss account.

  2. Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office needs to instruct GFS Back Office to reclass the amount from gain/loss account to the Retained Account GL, Interco Netting GL or Manual Intangible Asset GL, based on agreement with GFR Consolidation team or GFR Technical team. From receiving entity perspective, two steps are needed:

steps.title: Request capitalisation
steps.detail:
Business initiates the request for creation of a new intangible asset addition or capitalisation to Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office by providing the signed document of Legal Contract or AIN. AIN document is only applicable to deal value more than USD10 million.

Sample email is given below:

Upon receiving the request Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office requires to identify whether the Entity is maintaining Intangible Asset via subledger. If the entity do not have Subledger setting, Business, Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office require to raised manual journal and follow AZ Global Manual Journal Entry.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Complete external capitalisation template and obtain approval
steps.detail:
Business, Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office prepare Intangible Asset External Capitalisation Template and fill out all mandatory fields in the “Asset Creation Template” tab.

Prepare Intangible Asset External Capitalisation Template

Business, Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office to fill in all details for the asset based on instruction guidance listed at “Instruction Tab” and to identify whether the asset type is for;

New Intangible

New asset number field will be completed by GDO Back Office DMT team.

Addition Milestone Payment

New asset number field will be completed by Business, Embedded Finance or GFS Middle Office by referring back to previous email request on identifying the existing number created or contact Back Office R2R Fixed Asset team to provide Intangible Asset listing.

Provide supporting documents

Attached AIN & invoice supporting for supporting the capitalisation.

Task #

TASK NAME

steps.title: Initiate master data creation
steps.detail:
After ensuring all details are correct, Business, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office requests GDO Back Office DMT for creation of asset shell with the updated templates.

Send a request for asset shell creation

Once the Intangible Asset External Capitalisation Template is complete, send the completed template for approval based on approval matrix. Sample as per below;

Once approved, send an email request for a fixed asset creation to GDO Back Office DMT to process the request. A sample email request is shown below:

steps.detail:
Once Business, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office has submitted the request to create a new asset number, GDO Back Office DMT will create the asset shell in ERP system.

GDO Back Office DMT to verify that there is email approval attached by the respective approver, as per Approval Matrix. Sample as per below;

Open the Intangible Asset External Capitalisation Template from the attachment in the email request. Make sure the requester has filled out all mandatory fields (with asterisk ‘*’, highlighted in red) are complete in the “Asset Creation Template” tab.

Identify whether the Asset Creation Type is either;

New Intangible - refer to new asset creation.

Addition Milestone Payment - refer to new sub-asset creation.

New asset creation

Fill in the company code and asset numbers as per the request template (the fields “Asset Class” and “Company Code” in “Asset Creation Template” tab. “Number of similar assets” is “1” by default for a single asset creation).

steps.title: Raise InterCompany Request
steps.detail:
Upon receiving request from Business, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office is required to work together with Business, GFR Consolidation Team and GFR Technical team on understanding the content of the AIN/Legal document and any GAAP requirement. Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office will execute to transfer asset between legal entities in AZ, and need to follow as per AZ Global Intercompany Standard documented in Finance Library.

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office to prepare the expected Journal Entries and obtain an agreement with GFR Consolidation team or GFR Technical team.

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office to issue NTI (Non-Trade Intercompany Transactions) from Transferor (Selling Entity) to Transferee (Buying Entity) in NINTEX (Refer process 8.3.2.47 Intercompany Recharges for details).

From selling entity perspective, two steps are needed:

Retire the assets retirement by referring to 4.7.2 Intangible Asset Disposal or Retirement. Please refer to this process on detailed steps inclusive of what template to be used, who is the approver and how to check and obtain information from SAP. The asset of selling party will be retired from the FA register to gain / loss account.

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office needs to instruct GFS Back Office to reclass the amount from gain/loss account to the Retained Account GL, Interco Netting GL or Manual Intangible Asset GL, based on agreement with GFR Consolidation team or GFR Technical team. GFS Back Office Fixed Asset team needs to take note of this transaction to be able to report this under “F306 F306 - IC transfers in / (out)” in ERH MOT12 following ERH reporting timeline.

From receiving entity perspective, two steps are needed:

Capitalise the assets via 4.7.1 Process and Record Intangible Asset Additions. Please refer to this process on detailed steps inclusive of what template to be used, who is the approver and how to check or obtain information from SAP.

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office needs to inform GFS Back Office on which Credit GL to be used for the asset (eg. Retained Account GL, Interco Netting GL or Manual Intangible Asset GL), based on agreement GFR Consolidation team or GFR Technical team. GFS Back Office Fixed Asset team needs to take note of this transaction to be able to report this under “F306 F306 - IC transfers in / (out)” in ERH MOT12 following ERH reporting timeline.

## ## Process Detail The following step by step instructions explain how to perform the work involved in the process:
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.1

Execute Initial Depreciation mid-month (Test Run)
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

Prior to month end close, an initial depreciation test run is conducted at mid-month to help identify if there are any issues / errors to ensure resolution is in place. Mid-month test run is followed in all regions except NAM as NAM does not have mid-month schedule job run.

  1. Run Depreciation Test Run

Login to SAP.

Input SAP T-code AFAB and press Enter.

Please update the following fields:

  • Company Code

  • Fiscal Year: Current year

  • Posting Period: Current posting period

Tick “List assets”. Make sure that “Test Run” has also been ticked. Click on execute icon to proceed.

  1. Run Depreciation in Foreground and Background

Select between Option 1 or Option 2 to run depreciation:

Option 1: Running depreciation in Foreground if the number of fixed assets is low.
For Option 1, refer to sub-step B.1) Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file.

Option 2: Running depreciation in Background if the number of fixed assets is high. This option requires another T- code to view the result.
For Option 2, refer to sub-step B.2) Run Depreciation in Background.

B.1) Option 1: Run Depreciation in Foreground and update working file

At the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute” (or press F8 which performs the same function).

A pop up “Limitation online” will appear, warning that executing the Depreciation Run is limited to approximately 1000 assets. Click “Yes” to Proceed.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, there will be a statement highlighting “TESTRUN completed successfully” at the end of the page. If there are any errors, proceed to Step 4.7.2: 8.3.3.6.2 Investigate errors. The errors could be due to Cost Centres or Internal Orders being blocked.

Export the file to excel: Click on the Export to local file button (Or press F9).

Select the spreadsheet option and click on the green tick highlighted below.

Select the file path where you want to export and name the file, then click Generate. The report will be exported to excel.

Obtain the prior month’s working file of FA Movement and Analysis Template from the shared location. Please refer to Section 9 for the template to be used for FA Movement and analysis.

Save the previous month’s working file as the current month working file.

In the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis file, copy and replace the data from columns A to P in ‘AFAB last mth’ tab.

Then, go back to ‘AFAB’ tab and clear all data from columns B to P.

Next, open the depreciation posting run report which was previously generated and saved. Finally, copy the data into the cleared table in AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. Copy only into Column B to Column P (Grey Headers).

The columns with yellow headers either contain a formula or are for the report preparer’s remarks. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C.

B.2) Option 2: Run Depreciation in Background

Go to the top left of the page, go to “Program”, then select “Execute in Background” (or press F9).

A pop up “Background Print Parameters” will appear. Enter the Output Device as “local_en”. Click on the green tick to continue.

Another pop up will appear for the user’s information. Click on the green tick to continue.

The next pop up is to indicate when the job should run. In this instance, click on “Immediate” for immediate run, then click on Save (or Ctrl+S).

At the bottom of the page, the message “Background job was scheduled for program RAPOST20000” will appear.

  1. View depreciation job in SAP

To view the depreciation job, from any page in SAP Click on “System” > then select “Own Jobs”

On clicking on own jobs, the screen below will appear:

This is a Finished Job. It will be highlighted in green.

Make sure the Job has the green status: “Finished”. If it is not yet finished, the status will state “Active”. In that case simply keep refreshing the page periodically by clicking on the Refresh button (or “F8”).

If the job is finished, proceed to select the job, then click the Spool button.

Select the button, which will show the Spooled Depreciation Test Run result.

If the Depreciation Test Run is successful with no errors, the following screen will show:

Note: The report will only show the first 10 pages.

If the depreciation test run was unsuccessful, the following screen will be displayed.

Click on log box icon () to view error message and reason of the failed test run.

Generally – there are two reasons for failed test runs:

  • Posting to prior month which has already been posted, as shown in the screen below:

  • Posting to the subsequent month before the current period is posted, as shown in the screen below:

To view the full report, click on Settings as highlighted below:

In the pop up, change the Display area to show “From page” 1 to a sufficiently large number of pages to cover the whole report.

The warning below will pop-up as shown. Click on the green tick or press Enter.

Export the report and save it to a local file by clicking on .

Export the report

Select Text with Tabs and click on the green tick .

Select where the file is to be exported to and name the file, then click Generate.
The report will be exported.

Open the Excel File, which will appear as below:

Select all the rows. Then go to Data --> Text to Columns as highlighted below:

In the pop up, select “Fixed width” and click “Next”.

In the next screen, adjust the field widths according to the columns required in the Depreciation Analysis file by using the lines with arrows as shown below. After that, click “Finish”.

The data is now split as required. The data is now ready to be pasted into the AFAB Tab in the Depreciation Analysis file.

Copy the raw data into the AFAB tab in the Depreciation Analysis File. The data to be transferred should only be entered Column B to Column P. The formula in Column A is a concatenation of Column B and Column C. Make sure the formula is copied to cover all the asset lines.

Using Column A, the formula in Column Q will use VLOOKUP to “AFAB last month” tab’s Column A and Column N to get last month’s depreciation posted for the same asset.

The formula in Column R is the difference between Column N (amount to be posted) and Column Q (amount posted in previous month).

Go to column “H” in tab “Dep Analysis_RU10” and look at the variances.

Note: If the variance is more than USD 1m by account determination in “AFAB” tab or more than 5% in “Dep Analysis” tab column G, the processer needs to explain the reason of movement (i.e. sales of asset, etc.) in column S in “AFAB” tab.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.2

Investigate error
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office

GFS Back Office R2R needs to investigate errors in the depreciation run and liaise with the relevant teams, depending on the error's nature.

  1. Identify nature of error

While running the depreciation through the system, the user may encounter errors due to:

  • Technical Issues encountered in SAP

  • Other common issues (e.g. cost centre closed, insufficient master data entered)

  1. Escalate error

Once the root cause is determined, reach out to relevant parties who can assist with error resolution:

  • Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office for other common issues (Proceed to Step 4.7.3: 8.3.3.6.3 Assist with Issue resolution)

  • IT for technical issues (Proceed to Step 4.7.7: 8.3.3.6.7 Contact IT Help Desk and Raise Ticket)
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.3

Assist with Error Resolution
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office N/A GFS Back Office R2R

Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office will need to assist to resolve the issue. Generally, errors are due to Cost Centres or Internal Orders that were closed and need to be reopened for depreciation.

  1. Assist with error resolution

For common errors relating to blocked Cost Centres, check if the cost centre should be unblocked, or whether the asset should be transferred to a different cost centre. In both cases, contact GFS Back Office DMT which performs cost centre updates.

  1. Confirm if mid-month was run, and respond to GFS Back Office R2R

Once the error is resolved, revert to GFS Back Office R2R accordingly, who will proceed with options below (Please note this is not applicable for NAM as NAM does not follow mid-month schedule job run):

If mid-month test was conducted, proceed to Step 4.7.6: 8.3.3.6.6 Execute depreciation at month end (Test run).

If mid-month test was not yet conducted, proceed to Step 4.7.4: 8.3.3.6.4 All Asset Postings received (pre-month-end).
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.4

All Asset Postings received (Pre-month-end)
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

All fixed asset posting requests needs to be sent to GFS Back Office R2R as part of the pre-closing activities.

Obtain all asset postings: Markets to request asset transactions on or before the deadline as per the Global Close Calendar Standard. All postings received by the request deadline will need to be processed by the Back Office, prior to the asset posting deadline as per GCC. This covers requests for asset acquisition, scrapping, retirement, sale, impairment etc.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.5

Complete all asset postings
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

Perform all Fixed Asset Postings

All postings received by the requested deadline will need to be processed by the Back Office, prior to the asset posting deadline as per GCC.

This ensures that:

  • There are no pending requests to change Fixed Asset Cost Centres

  • All assets to be retired in that month and with the depreciation policy not to depreciate in the month of disposal have been processed before the Depreciation run
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.6

Execute Depreciation at month end (test run)
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

There will be another test run during month-end after all asset postings have been completed. The test run functionality of ERP is utilised. Any issues or errors encountered will have to be resolved before the depreciation run can be completed in production mode.

Note: Month end depreciation test run for NAM Hubs is performed with an automated background scheduled job on WD-4 (US time 22:00) on monthly basis.

To check the test run result from the scheduled background job, use T-code AFBP to check the posting log of schedule run.

At parameter in the below SAP screen, input Company Code, Fiscal Year and Posting Period. Tick on “SchedMan Monitor” – Schedule Manager: Monitor then click on execute .

Following screen displays all historical job logs. Double click on “ Depreciation posting run” entry and the status will change to “green” status which means posting run is completed without error.

The next panel will appear as below. Click on “Additional Info”, to confirm the company code, and posting period. Click on back icon to download the list of posting log.

On the next page, uncheck “SchedMan Monitor” and check on “List assets” . Click on execute icon to proceed.

The result of total depreciation posting will be displayed at the bottom of the report at column “Amount to be posted”. Take a copy of screenshot of the posting run result with time stamp as CPX011 control supporting. This screenshot is used to match the current month’s totals in the Dep Analysis tab in Depreciation variance analysis template. Refer sub-step 8.3.3.6.9 Perform Analysis on Depreciation.

Execute Depreciation Test Run

Execute Depreciation Test run as per month end closing schedule (WD – 2). Test run steps are similar to the mid-month depreciation test performed.

For detailed steps, please refer to Step 4.7.1: 8.3.3.6.1 Execute initial depreciation at mid-month.

If there are errors encountered while executing the test-run, proceed to Step 4.7.2: 8.3.3.6.2 Investigate error, to follow similar error resolution process as performed during mid-month test run.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.7

Contact IT Help Desk & Raise Ticket
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R IT N/A

If a technical issue is encountered during the run, GFS Back Office R2R will contact the IT help desk and raise a ticket for the case.

Raise Ticket to IT Help Desk

Go to web link: https://azprod.service-now.com/navpage.do

Raise a ticket according to technical issue faced, along with the relevant descriptions and supporting screenshots.
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.8

Resolve Error
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
IT IT N/A GFS Back Office R2R

IT supports the case until the technical error is resolved.

Resolve and respond to technical error raised

Support and close technical issue raised.

Once error has been resolved, respond to GFS Back Office R2R through email, who will then confirm if mid-month test run was conducted.

If mid-month test run was not yet conducted, GFS Back Office R2R to proceed with Step 4.7.4: 8.3.3.6.4 All asset postings received (pre-month-end).

If mid-month test run was conducted, GFS Back Office R2R to proceed with Step 4.7.6: 8.3.3.6.6 Execute depreciation at month end (Test run).
Task # TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.9

Perform variance analysis against prior month depreciation
Responsible Accountable Consulted Informed
GFS Back Office R2R GFS Back Office R2R N/A N/A

If there are no errors in the depreciation test run, GFS Back Office R2R will perform the analysis of the depreciation test run figures, comparing them with prior month depreciation figures. A review is performed of depreciation expenditure to ensure that the monthly cost is recorded accurately. Ensure you perform control CPX011 as per the FCAS framework for your unit.

Perform Analysis on Depreciation

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab of the FA Movement and Analysis Template, both month’s data (previous month and current month) will be derived from formulas in the table below, which represents the FA Sub ledger.

Last month (Col D): = SUMIF(‘AFAB last month!D:D,’Dep Analysis_RU10’!C110,’AFAB last month’!N:N).

This month (Col E) =SUMIF('AFAB_Current month'!D:D,'Dep Analysis_RU10'!C117,'AFAB_Current month'!N:N)

Column F is the Variance Value, and this is the difference between current month (Col E) and previous month (Col D).

Column G is the variance value in USD.

To determine the USD value of the variance in local currency, go to this link of Azure Lite website and scroll down to identify the budgeted rate for the currency of the market. For e.g. in the above report, the currency RUB is to be converted to USD currency.

Screen will appear as below after selecting below parameters in drop down:

Rate Type: Budget and Forecast rates

Year: Current year

Period: Current month

  1. Investigate and explain any variances

  1. Summarise the cause for depreciation variance

In the “Dep Analysis” Tab, there is a summary of the cause of variance which was encountered (illustrative purposes only).

Depreciation variances can be caused by many factors. Below is a list of common causes of depreciation variances:

Common causes of decreased depreciation:

  • Asset Retirements in the last month / current month

  • Assets fully depreciated in the last month

  • There was an unusually large depreciation amount for the last month (e.g. accelerated depreciation following an impairment review), so compared to the current month’s depreciation, it would appear to be low

Common causes of increased depreciation:

  • Asset Acquisitions / AUC Capitalisations in last month / current month

  • Assets with depreciation start dates brought forward / moved to an earlier date (resulting in an increased depreciation in the following months to normalise total depreciation value)

The table below indicates how to check for common causes of depreciation variances:

B.1) Increased Depreciation:

Common Causes How to Check for it Action Step
New Asset Capitalised during the month Go to SAP T-code AS03, and go to the General Tab. Check the field “Capitalised on date” No further action required
Depreciation start date brought forward Go to SAP T-code AS03, and view depreciation start date Verify with market if it was intended to bring forward the date

B.2) Decreased Depreciation:

Common Causes How to Check for it Action Step
Net book value is zero This can be checked by checking asset NBV in SAP T-code AW01N. No further action required
Unusually large depreciation in last month (special cases)

  • Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date (using SAP T-code AW01N) through Tab “Posted Value”

  • Check if the large depreciation value was due to change in useful life (Using SAP T-code AS03 through tab “Deprec. Area)

  • Check if last month’s increase was due to changes in the asset’s depreciation start date, caused by backdated depreciation (Using SAP T- code AW01N) through Tab “Parameters” check Ord.dep.start date and make comparison through tab “Comparison”

  • If there was a change in depreciation start date, the legitimacy of the change would have been verified in the previous month; hence no further action required

  • If there was a change in useful life, verify with the market whether this was intended

Depreciation is allocated by cost centre defined in the Asset Master Record. The processer will run depreciation for all active fixed assets on a monthly basis, as per the Global Close Calendar. The depreciation key defines the method that will be used to calculate depreciation for the asset.

Depreciation areas are set up to calculate depreciation for different purposes such as Group book, Local GAAP or Tax depreciation.

The output of the depreciation process will be the depreciation postings in each of the relevant depreciation areas, by the amount calculated as defined by the depreciation key. This will result in an adjustment of the Net Book Value of the Fixed Assets. Note that Group book and Local GAAP depreciation are posted to the General Ledger (GL) at the same time upon running AFAB whilst Tax depreciation is displayed in the AA module for reporting purposes.
